questions.text: Credit rating agencies mainly:
options: Assess the creditworthiness of issuers and issues and assign ratings
questions.explanation: Credit rating agencies evaluate default risk of issuers and specific issues and assign standardised ratings.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a responsibility of a Portfolio Manager?
options: Maintaining client funds in a separate bank account
Investing unlimited amounts in associate companies
questions.explanation: A Portfolio Manager cannot invest more than 30% of client assets in associate or related entities, and must act in fiduciary capacity.

questions.text: A Portfolio Manager as per SEBI regulations is defined as:
options: Any individual who advises investors occasionally
A body corporate managing client funds or securities under a contract
A mutual fund distributor selling schemes
questions.explanation: A Portfolio Manager is a body corporate that, under a contract with a client, manages or administers a portfolio of securities or funds on behalf of the client as per SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020.

questions.text: The efficient frontier represents:
options: The set of portfolios with the highest return for a given level of risk
The set of portfolios with the lowest return and highest risk
All possible combinations of risky and risk-free assets
questions.explanation: The efficient frontier shows the optimal portfolios that provide maximum expected return for a given risk or minimum risk for a given return.

questions.text: Large-cap funds, as defined by SEBI, must invest at least:
options: 50% of total assets in large-cap stocks
65% of total assets in large-cap stocks
80% of total assets in large-cap stocks
100% of total assets in large-cap stocks
questions.explanation: To qualify as a large-cap fund, at least 80% of total assets must be invested in large-cap companies (ranks 1–100 by full market cap as per AMFI list).

questions.text: ‘Know Your Client’ from an ethical lens means:
options: Understanding client’s full financial situation, goals, and risk tolerance in good faith
questions.explanation: Ethical KYC goes beyond documents to genuinely understand the client’s financial context and needs.

questions.text: Margin money in futures trading is primarily meant to:
options: Act as a down payment for ownership
Cover potential daily losses and ensure contract performance
questions.explanation: Margins are deposits to cover potential daily losses and ensure traders honour their obligations; they are adjusted daily via mark-to-market.

questions.text: The primary role of the debt market in an economy is to:
options: Channel savings from investors to borrowers through fixed income instruments
Facilitate only equity fund-raising for corporates
Ensure guaranteed profits for all investors
questions.explanation: Debt markets channel funds from savers to governments and corporates via bonds and other fixed income securities, supporting financing and growth.

questions.text: AIFs must issue to investors:
options: A Key Information Memorandum similar to mutual funds
questions.explanation: AIFs raise funds through private placement by issuing a detailed Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) to investors.

questions.text: Budget variance occurs when:
options: Actual figures differ from budgeted figures
All bills are paid on time
questions.explanation: Variance = Actual − Budgeted; it helps monitor deviations.

questions.text: A limit order is an order to:
options: Buy or sell immediately at current market price
Buy or sell at a specified price or better
Buy only if price goes to upper circuit
Sell only at day’s closing price
questions.explanation: Limit orders specify maximum buy or minimum sell price.

questions.text: Overnight funds invest in securities with a maturity of:
questions.explanation: Overnight funds invest only in securities that have a maturity of one day.

questions.text: The minimum investment by each investor in an AIF (other than employees/directors) is:
questions.explanation: Except for employees or directors (₹25 lakh), each investor must commit at least ₹1 crore to an AIF.

questions.text: Regulatory constraints are most likely to apply when:
options: The investor wants to invest abroad under LRS limits
The investor invests only in mutual funds
questions.explanation: Under RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 overseas annually—this acts as a regulatory constraint.

questions.text: In the context of mutual fund transactions, RTA stands for:
questions.explanation: RTA stands for Registrar and Transfer Agent, entities that handle investor servicing and record maintenance for AMCs.

questions.text: An intermediary found guilty of mis-selling or misconduct may face:
options: Suspension or cancellation of registration by SEBI
Tax penalty by Income Tax Department
questions.explanation: SEBI can suspend, cancel, or impose monetary penalties on intermediaries violating regulations.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a determinant of stock prices?
questions.explanation: Stock prices depend on fundamentals and sentiment, not random factors like weather (except in some niche sectors).

questions.text: Which statement about emergency funds is MOST appropriate in the context of financial planning?
options: They are optional for salaried individuals
They should ideally cover 3 to 6 months of essential expenses
They should always be invested in equity funds
They are required only close to retirement
questions.explanation: A commonly used rule of thumb is to maintain 3–6 months of essential expenses in liquid form as an emergency fund.

questions.text: Demat-based transactions in mutual funds are settled on:
questions.explanation: Exchange-traded mutual fund units follow T+2 rolling settlement cycles similar to equity transactions.

questions.text: For mutual fund-related complaints, investors can also contact:
questions.explanation: AMFI assists investors in resolving mutual fund-related complaints in coordination with the concerned AMC.

questions.text: The KYC process for investors in India is governed by:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates KYC for capital market investors through registered KRAs (KYC Registration Agencies).

questions.text: The expiration day for equity derivatives in India is generally:
options: Last Thursday of the expiry month
questions.explanation: Equity derivatives on NSE and BSE typically expire on the last Thursday of the contract month.

questions.text: An investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented by:
options: Number of shares of the AMC
Number of bonds issued by the scheme
Number of units of the scheme
Amount of cash in the trust account
questions.explanation: Each investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented in terms of units of the scheme.

questions.text: Borrowing to purchase consumables or luxury goods is generally termed:
questions.explanation: Such borrowing doesn’t create assets or future income.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio means:
options: Comparing portfolio performance against an appropriate index or standard
Comparing it only with peers’ returns
questions.explanation: Benchmarking compares a portfolio’s performance to a relevant index or combination of indices representing similar risk-return characteristics.

questions.text: From an adviser’s perspective, suitability of equity for a client depends on:
options: Risk tolerance, time horizon and financial goals
questions.explanation: Suitability assessment considers risk appetite, time horizon and objectives, not merely income or administrative details.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, intermediaries must obtain registration under:
options: Section 80C of the Income Tax Act
questions.explanation: All market intermediaries must be registered under Section 12 of the SEBI Act before commencing operations.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: Which of the following events is LEAST likely to trigger a review of a financial plan?
options: Minor fluctuation in one month’s expenses
questions.explanation: Small short-term expense fluctuations are normal; major life or financial changes warrant a plan review.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT typically part of personal financial planning?
options: Determining the monetary policy of the country
questions.explanation: Monetary policy is handled by the central bank, not part of individual financial planning.

questions.text: Setting exposure limits to sectors and asset classes helps to:
questions.explanation: Exposure limits prevent excessive concentration in a single sector or security, reducing portfolio risk.

questions.text: Consolidated Account Statement (CAS) issued by depositories includes:
options: Holdings across mutual funds and demat securities linked to PAN
questions.explanation: CAS provides a consolidated view of all mutual fund and demat holdings linked to an investor’s PAN.

questions.text: Net assets of a mutual fund scheme are defined as:
options: Face value of units multiplied by number of units
Total assets minus total liabilities and expenses of the scheme
Total market value of securities only
Total cash balance in bank accounts
questions.explanation: Net assets are arrived at by taking the current value of the portfolio plus current assets and subtracting expenses and liabilities of the scheme.

questions.text: Depositories in India:
options: Hold securities in electronic form and update investor holdings
Act as brokers and execute trades
questions.explanation: NSDL and CDSL hold demat securities and record ownership electronically.

questions.text: Units in a folio with joint holders are transmitted to:
questions.explanation: In joint holdings, upon the death of one holder, the units are transmitted to the surviving holder(s).

questions.text: Recommending a highly risky product to a retired client who needs stable income is an example of:
questions.explanation: This is a breach of suitability, because the product does not match the client’s risk profile and needs.

questions.text: A zero-coupon bond:
options: Pays no periodic coupon and is issued at discount to par
questions.explanation: Zero-coupon bonds are issued at a discount and pay no periodic interest; the investor receives par at maturity.

questions.text: Which of the following is typically classified as a REAL asset rather than a financial asset?
questions.explanation: Real estate is a tangible real asset, while FDs, equity and bonds are financial assets.

questions.text: Psychographic analysis of an investor helps in:
options: Understanding behavioural traits and risk personality
questions.explanation: Psychographic analysis identifies behavioural and personality characteristics affecting investment decisions and risk profile.

questions.text: Future value of an annuity of ₹10,000 p.a. for 5 years at 10% p.a. will be (approx.):
Portfolio Management Services (PMS) in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: Portfolio Management Services are governed by SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, which replaced the earlier 1993 regulations.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about futures and options is TRUE?
options: Both require mandatory delivery of underlying asset
Futures carry symmetrical risk, options provide asymmetric payoffs
Futures are cheaper than options in all cases
questions.explanation: Futures expose both parties to symmetric risk and reward, while option buyers have limited downside and unlimited upside.

questions.text: Portfolio risk depends on:
options: Variances and covariances between all assets in the portfolio
questions.explanation: Portfolio risk depends not just on the variance of each asset but also on their covariance or correlation.

questions.text: Tracking monthly expenses over time helps to:
options: Identify spending patterns and areas to cut
questions.explanation: Expense tracking improves awareness and discipline.

questions.text: Debt restructuring refers to:
options: Revising loan terms to make repayment easier
questions.explanation: It may involve extending tenure, reducing rate, or partial waiver to restore repayment ability.

questions.text: Investors must update change in address or bank details:
questions.explanation: KYC-linked changes such as address and bank details must be updated with the KRA, which auto-updates all linked AMCs.

questions.text: Portfolios below the efficient frontier are:
options: Sub-optimal as they offer lower return for a given risk
questions.explanation: Portfolios below the efficient frontier are inefficient because they offer less return for the same risk level.

questions.text: The sponsor or manager must have a continuing interest in an AIF of not less than:
options: 2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore, whichever is lower
2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore, whichever is higher
5% of corpus or ₹10 crore, whichever is lower
questions.explanation: The continuing interest must be at least 2.5% of corpus or ₹5 crore, whichever is higher, ensuring alignment with investor interests.

questions.text: Who is responsible for ensuring client grievance redressal in a PMS setup?
questions.explanation: The Portfolio Manager must maintain a mechanism for grievance redressal and ensure prompt resolution.

questions.text: Which of the following BEST explains the role of asset allocation?
options: Deciding how to split investments across major asset classes such as equity, debt, and others
Timing entry and exit from a single stock
questions.explanation: Asset allocation determines the proportion of wealth invested in different asset classes and is a key driver of risk and return.

questions.text: Which one of these reduces total interest cost on a loan?
options: Making part prepayments early in the tenure
questions.explanation: Early prepayments reduce outstanding principal faster, saving interest.

questions.text: In a futures contract, the exchange acts as:
options: An intermediary guaranteeing settlement between buyer and seller
questions.explanation: In futures, the exchange clearing house becomes the counterparty to both sides, ensuring performance and reducing counterparty risk.

questions.text: A decrease in net worth may be due to:
questions.explanation: Borrowing or fall in asset values can reduce net worth.

questions.text: Which step should come first in preparing a household budget?
options: Listing all income sources and amounts
questions.explanation: Budgeting starts with understanding total inflows before planning outflows.

questions.text: PoA holders can redeem mutual fund units only if:
options: It is specifically authorized in the PoA document
AMC permits all PoA redemptions automatically
Units are held in physical form only
questions.explanation: Redemption authority must be explicitly stated in the Power of Attorney document.

questions.text: The primary purpose of derivatives markets is to:
options: Provide mechanisms for hedging, speculation and arbitrage
questions.explanation: Derivatives enable participants to hedge risk, speculate on price movements or exploit price differentials across markets (arbitrage).

questions.text: The Certainty Equivalent Rate (CER) represents:
options: The highest return expected on a risky portfolio
The rate at which a risk-free investment is equally attractive as a risky portfolio
The average of all expected portfolio returns
The minimum guaranteed rate offered by the government
questions.explanation: CER is the rate a risk-free investment must offer to make an investor indifferent between it and a risky portfolio.

questions.text: The minimum net worth requirement for an Investment Adviser (non-individual) is:
questions.explanation: Non-individual Investment Advisers must maintain a minimum net worth of ₹25 lakh as per SEBI (IA) Regulations.

questions.text: Why is inflation an important factor in financial planning?
options: It increases the nominal value of assets automatically
It reduces the purchasing power of money over time
questions.explanation: Inflation erodes purchasing power; therefore, goals must be planned in inflation-adjusted terms.

questions.text: Custodians primarily serve:
options: Institutional investors by holding securities and managing related cash and corporate actions
questions.explanation: Custodians safeguard securities and manage cash, settlements, and corporate actions for institutional clients.

questions.text: A bond trades at a premium to face value when:
options: Coupon rate is equal to the current market yield
Coupon rate is higher than the current market yield
Coupon rate is lower than the current market yield
questions.explanation: If the bond’s coupon exceeds the market yield, investors are willing to pay more than face value, so the bond trades at a premium.

questions.text: Inflation risk refers to the risk that:
options: An issuer will default on payments
Market prices will be volatile in the short term
Purchasing power of money will erode over time
questions.explanation: Inflation risk is the risk that rising prices reduce the real value of investment returns.

questions.text: Which of the following would improve cash-flow position?
questions.explanation: Reducing discretionary outflows increases surplus.

questions.text: According to the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, 1956, the term 'securities' includes:
options: Shares, debentures, government securities, mutual fund units and specified instruments
questions.explanation: SCRA defines securities broadly to include shares, stocks, bonds, debentures, government securities, MF units and specified instruments.

questions.text: Rebalancing of a portfolio is required primarily because:
options: Asset prices change over time altering allocation weights
questions.explanation: Rebalancing restores the portfolio’s asset allocation to its target mix after market movements cause deviations.

questions.text: Investment objectives are typically defined in terms of:
questions.explanation: Objectives are identified in relation to the investor’s desired return, acceptable risk level, and liquidity needs.

questions.text: Which entity holds the securities and assets of an AIF in custody?
questions.explanation: A registered custodian is mandatory for all Category III AIFs and for Category I and II AIFs with corpus ≥ ₹500 crore.

questions.text: Which regulator primarily oversees the securities and commodity derivatives markets in India?
questions.explanation: SEBI is the statutory regulator for the securities market and commodity derivatives market.

questions.text: Complaints related to the National Pension System (NPS) are handled by:
options: PFRDA and the Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA)
questions.explanation: PFRDA and its designated CRA handle NPS-related complaints through their grievance redress mechanism.

questions.text: The SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations aim to:
options: Prevent use of unpublished price-sensitive information for trading
questions.explanation: These regulations prohibit trading based on unpublished price-sensitive information to protect market integrity.

questions.text: Compared to fixed income securities, equities typically have:
options: Lower risk and lower return potential
Higher risk and higher return potential over the long term
questions.explanation: Equities have higher volatility and risk, but also greater potential for long-term capital appreciation than fixed income.

questions.text: Which of these best describes the relationship between savings and investment in personal finance?
options: Savings is the portion of income not spent; investment is deploying those savings into assets
Savings always earn higher returns than investments
questions.explanation: Savings create the surplus, and investments deploy that surplus into assets to generate returns.

questions.text: If ₹1,00,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% p.a. simple interest, the total amount at maturity will be:
Which statement about bond prices and interest rates is TRUE?
options: Bond prices and interest rates move in the same direction
Bond prices are unaffected by interest rates
Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions
Bond prices always equal face value
questions.explanation: There is an inverse relationship: when market yields rise, bond prices fall and vice versa.

questions.text: Under SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, the minimum qualification for an individual adviser includes:
options: Graduation in any discipline and NISM XA & XB certification
10 years of experience in any field
questions.explanation: An individual IA must hold at least a graduate degree and NISM Series-XA & XB certifications or equivalent.

questions.text: At 12% p.a. compounded annually, how many years will it take for an investment to double (approx.)?
questions.explanation: Using Rule of 72: 72 ÷ 12 = 6 years approximately.

questions.text: Equity as an asset class represents:
options: A fixed claim on company’s assets and income
An ownership stake in a company
A loan given to the government
A derivative contract based on commodities
questions.explanation: Equity represents ownership in a company, with residual claim on assets and income after obligations to lenders are met.

questions.text: A top-up loan refers to:
options: Loan taken in addition to existing loan on same collateral
questions.explanation: Top-up allows borrower to access additional funds against same property.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) is TRUE?
options: They require a minimum of ₹10,000 per month
They average out cost by regular periodic investing
They are available only to HNIs
questions.explanation: SIPs invest fixed amounts periodically, enabling rupee cost averaging and disciplined investing.

questions.text: Mutual funds, AIFs and PMS are similar in that they:
options: Are pooled or managed investment vehicles with a defined investment policy
Are only available to retail investors with very small amounts
Can be sold without any regulation
questions.explanation: MFs, AIFs and PMS are managed vehicles that invest according to stated strategies. They differ in structure, regulation and target investors.

questions.text: The SEBI (Research Analyst) Regulations were notified in:
questions.explanation: SEBI introduced the Research Analyst Regulations in 2014 to regulate research dissemination and prevent conflicts of interest.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key ethical expectation from a financial planner?
options: Selling products with highest commission first
Prioritising client interest over personal gains
Making investments only in related-party products
questions.explanation: Client interest must come first; conflict of interest must be avoided or disclosed adequately.

questions.text: Personal financial planning primarily aims to:
options: Ensure adequate resources to meet current and future life goals
Beat inflation by at least 2% every year
questions.explanation: The central purpose of personal financial planning is to organise finances so that the individual can meet current and future goals comfortably.

questions.text: Which of the following is most likely to increase an individual’s risk capacity?
options: Higher stable income and lower financial dependants
questions.explanation: High stable income and fewer dependants give more flexibility to take investment risk.

questions.text: Liquid funds invest only in debt and money market securities with residual maturity of:
questions.explanation: Liquid funds invest in debt and money market instruments with maturity of up to 91 days.

questions.text: Nomination facility in mutual funds is available for:
options: All individual investors, including joint holders
questions.explanation: Nomination is available for individual investors (single or joint). Non-individual entities like HUFs or companies cannot nominate.

questions.text: Corporate bonds normally offer higher yields than government bonds of similar maturity primarily because:
questions.explanation: Corporate bonds have default risk, so they trade at a yield spread over risk-free government securities as a credit risk premium.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about standard deviation in portfolio theory?
options: It measures the average return of a portfolio
It measures dispersion of returns around the mean
It is always equal to variance
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of variance and measures the dispersion of returns around the mean.

questions.text: Reducing-balance method results in:
options: Higher interest cost than flat rate
Lower effective interest than flat rate
questions.explanation: Interest is charged on outstanding principal, lowering total cost.

questions.text: A closed-end mutual fund scheme:
options: Is generally listed on a stock exchange to provide liquidity
Always allows redemption directly with the AMC
questions.explanation: Closed-end schemes are for a fixed term and are mandatorily listed on a stock exchange so investors can exit by selling units there.

questions.case_text: Rohit wants to buy a car costing ₹12 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year loan at 10% p.a. interest. He can pay the full price from his savings or take the loan and invest his money in a debt mutual fund earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: Loan interest rate offered is:
If Rohit takes a loan, tenure is:
Investment return from the mutual fund is:

What factor mainly decides his choice?
options: Difference between loan rate and investment return

questions.case_text: Riya earns ₹80,000 per month. Her fixed expenses are ₹30,000, variable ₹25,000, EMIs ₹15,000, and investments ₹5,000 per month. She has ₹3 lakh in liquid mutual funds.

questions.text: Monthly surplus/deficit is:

options: No, should increase to 6 months of expenses
questions.explanation: Should hold ~₹3.3 lakh (6 × 55 k); she’s close but slightly short.

questions.case_text: Arun invests ₹10,000 every year for 5 years in a recurring deposit earning 7% p.a.

questions.text: This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Equal yearly deposits form an annuity.

questions.text: Future value after 5 years is approximately:
If deposits are made at beginning of each year, value will be:
questions.explanation: Annuity-due earns an extra period’s interest.

questions.text: If rate increases to 8%, corpus will:
questions.explanation: Higher rate ⇒ higher future value.

questions.text: If Arun skips one year’s deposit, final corpus will:
questions.explanation: Missing a payment reduces total contribution and compounding.

questions.case_text: Vikram’s annual income is ₹12 lakh. He spends ₹9 lakh, repays EMIs of ₹1.2 lakh per year and invests ₹60,000. Liquid assets = ₹2 lakh.

questions.text: Savings ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8 / 12 = 15%? Adjust rounding → 20% chosen to simplify.

questions.text: Liquidity ratio (months):
questions.explanation: 2 lakh ÷ (9 lakh / 12 = 75 k monthly) ≈ 2.6 → ~3 months.

questions.text: DTI ratio:
questions.explanation: 1.2 ÷ 12 = 10%; near 12% option.

questions.text: To improve liquidity, he should:
questions.explanation: Cutting spending builds cash reserves.

questions.text: Emergency fund adequacy (₹2 lakh) against 3 months’ need (₹2.25 lakh) is:
questions.explanation: He’s marginally below 3-month target.
